findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for SpawnProcess (verified issubclass is False), so a hung/dead flusher is silently never killed on restart, which is a regression from the old unconditional kill().

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:259 — Because the old process is not killed, a slow flusher that is only "hung" (e.g. blocked in future.result()) resumes next to its replacement on the same shards, producing duplicate segments and writing to the same healthy_since/backpressure Values, which hides the replacement's health; orphans pile up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — join() breaks once the deadline passes and skips every remaining process, and the isinstance check at line 346 never matches SpawnProcess anyway, so on rebalance the old flushers keep running unterminated while new flushers for the reassigned shards start.

src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — --flusher-processes has no range check: a negative value makes num_processes negative, so process_to_shards_map is empty and i % num_processes raises KeyError at startup, and 0 silently means one process per shard.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:301 — Each per-process SpansBuffer is expected to report memory for the whole Redis cluster rather than per shard (buffer.py is not in this snapshot), so memory info is fetched N times on every submit: the used/available ratio stays the same but Redis INFO load grows N-fold.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for SpawnProcess (verified issubclass is False), so a hung/dead flusher is silently never killed on restart, which is a regression from the old unconditional kill().

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:259 — Because the old process is not killed, a slow flusher that is only "hung" (e.g. blocked in future.result()) resumes next to its replacement on the same shards, producing duplicate segments and writing to the same healthy_since/backpressure Values, which hides the replacement's health; orphans pile up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index.

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on an unhealthy "hang" it restarts by calling `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` but only attempts to kill the old worker when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (i.e., it does nothing for the `threading.Thread` case used when `produce_to_pipe is not None`). Since the old thread is not stopped/joined and `self.processes[process_index]` is simply overwritten, the original thread can continue running (or resume later) on the same shards, leading to duplicate flushing/producing. Additionally, both old and new threads share the same `mp_context.Value` objects from `process_healthy_since` / `process_backpressure_since`, so the old thread can keep updating these and mask the replacement’s health, and repeated restarts can leak orphan threads up to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` per index.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — join() breaks once the deadline passes and skips every remaining process, and the isinstance check at line 346 never matches SpawnProcess anyway, so on rebalance the old flushers keep running unterminated while new flushers for the reassigned shards start.

src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — --flusher-processes has no range check: a negative value makes num_processes negative, so process_to_shards_map is empty and i % num_processes raises KeyError at startup, and 0 silently means one process per shard.

adjudication.rationale: The new click option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no validation, and the value is passed through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means negative values are accepted (truthy) and `0` is treated as “unset”. With a negative `max_processes`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative, so `process_to_shards_map` is built from `range(self.num_processes)` as an empty dict, then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` yields keys not present and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]` raises `KeyError` during initialization. With `0`, the `or` makes it behave like defaulting to `len(assigned_shards)` (one process per shard), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:301 — Each per-process SpansBuffer is expected to report memory for the whole Redis cluster rather than per shard (buffer.py is not in this snapshot), so memory info is fetched N times on every submit: the used/available ratio stays the same but Redis INFO load grows N-fold.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes memory sampling from a single call (`self.buffer.get_memory_info()`) to iterating all per-process buffers and calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` for each (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`). This is verifiably N calls per submit now. Whether those calls are redundant (i.e., each returns whole-cluster Redis INFO rather than shard-scoped info) can’t be confirmed from this diff alone, but the change does introduce a potential N-fold increase in Redis INFO load/perf cost without changing the decision logic (still sums used/available).

tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:115 — test_flusher_processes_limit only checks constructor attributes (max_processes == 2 is tautological) and never submits spans, checks for even shard distribution, or checks that any flusher is alive or flushes, so it passes even if every flusher crashes on start.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions mostly validate internal bookkeeping set up during construction (`flusher.max_processes == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, `len(flusher.processes) == 2`) after passing `flusher_processes=2` into `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`. The test never checks `process.is_alive()` for the created processes/threads, never drives any flushing (no spans/messages submitted), and only checks total shard assignment (`total_shards == 4`) rather than distribution across processes. Given `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` adds a process/thread to `self.processes` immediately after `process.start()`, the test could still pass even if those workers crash immediately on startup or never flush anything. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in coverage of the newly added multiprocessing/shard-mapping logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127 — _create_process_for_shard is never called (dead code), and none of the new restart, per-process backpressure or kill paths are covered by tests, so the SpawnProcess kill regression passes CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` in `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, but there is no call site in the shown changes (restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` instead). That makes `_create_process_for_shard` dead/unreferenced code as far as this diff shows. Also, the new per-process restart/kill paths and per-process backpressure logic (e.g., `_ensure_processes_alive` with `process.kill()` and `process_restarts[process_index]`, and iterating `process_backpressure_since.values()` in `submit`) are not directly exercised by the added tests: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts process counts and shard distribution, and the existing flusher test was only updated to check `any(...)` backpressure values, not the restart/kill behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:65 — a negative --flusher-processes makes num_processes negative, leaving process_to_shards_map empty so i % num_processes indexes a missing key (KeyError); 0 silently means one process per shard instead of being rejected

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.__init__, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats negative ints as truthy, so `max_processes=-1` yields `self.max_processes=-1`. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative, `range(self.num_processes)` produces an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` (0 for -1) and attempts `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)`, raising KeyError. Also `max_processes=0` is falsy so it falls back to `len(assigned_shards)`, i.e. one process per shard, rather than rejecting 0. The click option added (`type=int`) shows no validation preventing these values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62 — the added time.sleep(0.1) "give flusher threads time" is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a lambda, so the race between join() setting stopped and flushers observing the new drift is still there

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to `lambda _: None` near the top of the test, and later the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` is intended to “Give flusher threads time to process”. Because of the monkeypatch, that sleep is a no-op and cannot provide any delay, so the change does not achieve its stated purpose and any race it was meant to mitigate would still exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — New `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard is always False for spawn-context SpawnProcess (verified: not a subclass), so hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, and the `AttributeError` catch is dead

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, processes are created via `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process` (i.e., the spawn-context process class). The restart path then conditionally calls `process.kill()` only under `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):`. This check is against the top-level `multiprocessing.Process` type, not the spawn-context process type used for creation, so the guard can fail for the spawned processes and skip `kill()` when a process is hung (the `hang` cause branch). The code then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, potentially leaving the hung process running while starting a replacement. This is a real behavioral defect risk grounded in the diff’s mismatch between creation type (`mp_context.Process`) and the `isinstance` guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127 — _create_process_for_shard` has no callers and is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff adds a helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int): ...` that searches `process_to_shards_map` and then calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. Within the shown diff, all restarts are performed via `_ensure_processes_alive()` which directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and there are no references to `_create_process_for_shard` elsewhere. This makes the method dead/unused in the PR as shown—non-breaking, but it’s extra code that could be removed or wired up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:93 — Flusher builds its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` and uses the injected buffer only for `assigned_shards`, which ties it to the SpansBuffer constructor signature and drops any other config on the injected buffer

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__` no longer stores/uses the injected `buffer` (the prior `self.buffer = buffer` is removed) and instead creates new buffers per process via `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` inside `_create_process_for_shards`, using the injected buffer only to read `buffer.assigned_shards` (and to compute `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`). This does couple the flusher to the `SpansBuffer` constructor and risks dropping any non-shard configuration/state that may have been present on the injected instance. Whether that is an actual runtime defect depends on what `SpansBuffer` encapsulates beyond shard assignment, which is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:68 — Five parallel dicts keyed by process_index (processes, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts, buffers) plus process_to_shards_map track per-process state that belongs in one per-process record

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces multiple parallel dicts keyed by `process_index` in `SpanFlusher.__init__` (`self.processes`, `self.process_healthy_since`, `self.process_backpressure_since`, `self.process_restarts`, `self.buffers`) alongside `self.process_to_shards_map`. This is not a correctness defect by itself, but it is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue created by the change: per-process state is now spread across several structures and must be kept in sync across methods like `_ensure_processes_alive`, `_create_process_for_shards`, `submit`, and `join`, increasing the risk of future inconsistency. A per-process record/object would centralize this state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — CLI `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, but factory/flusher default None means one process per shard, and the help text says "Maximum ... Defaults to 1", so production and direct callers get different behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `--flusher-processes` is added with `default=1` in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py`, while `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` defaults `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passes it through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `None` means “one process per shard”, not 1. Thus CLI-invoked behavior (defaults to 1) differs from direct construction behavior (defaults to per-shard). This is a real, diff-grounded consistency/documentation issue, but not provably a functional defect without knowing intended defaults for non-CLI callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:32 — Docstring says "Creates one process per shard" but shards are grouped round-robin into at most max_processes processes

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the class docstring was changed to say it "Creates one process per shard". But the implementation explicitly caps process count via `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and then assigns shards round-robin with `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, meaning multiple shards can share a single process when `max_processes < len(assigned_shards)`. This is a real, diff-grounded documentation inconsistency, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199 — Metric tag key is "shards" here but "shard" at lines 185/195/244 (where 244 uses a single shard int, not the joined list), so per-shard dashboards get inconsistent tag keys

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.main, metric tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use tag key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. Elsewhere, `_ensure_processes_alive` increments `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` with `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}` (single int). This diff-grounded inconsistency will split metrics across different tag keys and break/complicate per-shard dashboards/alerts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:222 — if not process: continue` is dead because `processes` only ever holds started Process/Thread objects

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, `self.processes` is populated only in `_create_process_for_shards` with a `Process`/`Thread` object after `process.start()`, and the diff shows no code path that inserts `None`/falsy values into `self.processes`. So `if not process: continue` is redundant/dead, but it’s just a minor style nit rather than a real defect or substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:235 — Comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" is wrong: the check is per-process, not per-shard (same for "Update healthy_since for all shards" at line 178)

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out mismatched comments in `SpanFlusher.main` ("Update healthy_since for all shards...") and `_ensure_processes_alive` ("Check if any shard..."). The diff shows `healthy_since`/backpressure are tracked per spawned process via `process_healthy_since[process_index]`, and the hang check is purely `time.time() - process_healthy_since[...]`. So the comments are arguably inaccurate, but this is a documentation nit and does not indicate a functional defect or behavior that the code does not implement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:70 — healthy_since is set to time.time() at construction and then immediately reset in `_create_process_for_shards` (line 90), so the first init is redundant

adjudication.rationale: In the new code, `process_healthy_since` values are initialized in `__init__` to `int(time.time())`, and then each is reset again in `_create_process_for_shards` before starting the process. That does make the initial value redundant, but it’s a minor cleanup/style nit (no functional defect) and not an important review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337 — In the join loop, `process_index` is unused and the `remaining_time` early-break just repeats the deadline check in the inner while

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, `process_index` is indeed unused, but that’s a minor style/nit issue, not a defect. The `remaining_time`/early-break check is not a verifiable bug either: the inner `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time())` only controls waiting for the current process, while the outer break prevents iterating further once the deadline is exceeded. At most this is arguable redundancy/cleanliness, not a correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62 — time.sleep(0.1)` "give flusher threads time" does nothing because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CLAUDE.md:449 — An unrelated CLAUDE.md anti-pattern edit (hasattr vs isinstance) is bundled into the span flusher feature change

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an added documentation snippet in `CLAUDE.md` (around the shown hunk after the prefetch_related example) introducing a new anti-pattern note about `hasattr()` vs `isinstance()` for unions. This change is unrelated to the main code changes implementing multi-process span flushing (`src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, factory/CLI options, and tests). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context SpawnProcess, so hung flusher processes are never killed on restart (regression from the old unconditional kill()), leaking up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS duplicate processes per shard group that keep flushing the same Redis shards

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive(), processes are created via self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn") and make_process = self.mp_context.Process, so the stored objects are spawn-context processes (hinted as multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess in self.processes). On restart, the code only calls process.kill() when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) (and similarly terminate() in join). If SpawnProcess is not an instance of multiprocessing.Process (default-context Process), the kill/terminate path is skipped, and _create_process_for_shards() starts a new process while the old hung one can keep running, leading to duplicate flushers for the same shard group until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:301 — get_memory_info() is now called once per per-process buffer on every submit(); each call queries INFO across the whole shared Redis cluster, so round trips scale N-fold with flusher processes and used/available are counted N times

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit(), the diff changes from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to iterating all per-process buffers and calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` for each (see added loop building `memory_infos`). This makes the number of `get_memory_info()` invocations scale with `len(self.buffers)`/`num_processes`, which is a concrete performance/overhead concern introduced by the change. However, the claim that each call queries `INFO` across the whole shared Redis cluster and that used/available are “counted N times” cannot be verified from this diff because `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` implementation is not shown; the aggregation could be correct or could double-count depending on that hidden implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — When max_processes is None (the factory default), the flusher spawns one spawn-context process per assigned partition, each importing Sentry/Django and opening its own Kafka producer and Redis pool; the CLI defaults to 1, so the defaults disagree and memory/connection use scales with partition count

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real default mismatch: `SpanFlusher.__init__` sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so when `max_processes` is `None` (the factory default: `flusher_processes: int | None = None` in `factory.py`), it will create one process/thread per assigned shard/partition. Separately, the CLI option added in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py` sets `--flusher-processes` default to `1`, implying a different default behavior when invoked via CLI. The claim about per-process import/connection overhead is not directly verifiable from the shown diff, but the process-per-shard default and the CLI/factory default disagreement are.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:185 — Metric tag values are the joined shard list (for example "0,1,2,...,N"), which changes with every rebalance assignment, so timers and timings get unbounded tag cardinality; the key is also inconsistent ("shard" vs "shards" at line 199)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff introduces `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and uses it as a metrics tag value (e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`). This value depends on the current shard assignment (`shards` list) and thus can vary across rebalances, creating many distinct tag values (high/unbounded cardinality). The diff also shows an inconsistent tag key: `{"shard": shard_tag}` for `flusher.produce`/`segment_size_bytes` vs `{"shards": shard_tag}` for `flusher.wait_produce`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/metrics issue, not a correctness defect in the flusher logic itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:269 — record_stored_segments() now runs as one Redis pipeline per process buffer on every submit() instead of one batched call, adding N-1 extra round trips on the consumer path

adjudication.rationale:
In SpanFlusher.submit(), the diff changes a single call `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to a loop over all per-process buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`.
That clearly increases the number of `record_stored_segments()` invocations per submit from 1 to `len(self.buffers)` (i.e., number of flusher processes). If `record_stored_segments()` performs a Redis pipeline/round-trip (not shown in the diff but implied by the component), this would add extra Redis operations on the consumer path. This is a performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — join() breaks out of the loop once the deadline passes and skips terminate() for the remaining processes, leaving flusher processes and their Redis/Kafka connections alive across rebalances while a new SpanFlusher spawns more

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — The new `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard is always False for spawn-context `SpawnProcess`, so hung flusher processes are no longer killed on restart; the old process keeps running and a replacement is started on the same shards, which leaks processes and can produce duplicate flushes (the old code called `kill()` unconditionally).

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` the restart path only calls `process.kill()` under `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):` (and similarly `terminate()` in `join`). But processes are created via `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, producing a spawn-context `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` is not necessarily an instance of `multiprocessing.Process` (it is a sibling class under the context API), so this guard can evaluate False and skip killing the unhealthy process. The code then immediately starts a replacement via `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, which would leave the old process running on the same shards, leaking processes and risking duplicate flushing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:259 — Because the hung process is never killed, the replacement shares the same `stopped`, `healthy_since` and `backpressure_since` Values; when the old process recovers, both write the same health and backpressure state and flush the same shards at the same time.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, on an unhealthy cause (including `hang`) the code restarts via `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` but only attempts to kill the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. When `produce_to_pipe` is set, workers are `threading.Thread` (see `_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = threading.Thread`), which cannot be killed here, so the old hung thread keeps running while a new thread is started for the same `process_index`/`shards`. The restarted thread reuses the same shared `stopped` and `current_drift` values and the same per-process `process_healthy_since[...]` / `process_backpressure_since[...]` Values (they are created once in `__init__` and passed into `main` on every restart), so both threads can concurrently update health/backpressure state and flush the same shards, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346 — process.terminate()` in `join()` never runs for `SpawnProcess` because the same wrong isinstance check is used, so flushers still running after the join deadline are never terminated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `join()` using `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()` after waiting (and similarly `kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive`). But the finding’s claim that this “never runs for SpawnProcess” is not verifiable from the diff alone: the code previously used the same `isinstance(..., multiprocessing.Process)` check with `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, implying it was already intended to match spawn-context processes. The diff does not demonstrate that `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` fails this `isinstance` check, so asserting it never terminates is a speculative misread rather than a diff-proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — In `join()`, once the deadline passes the loop `break`s, so every remaining process is skipped without a stop or terminate attempt and is left running when the strategy is torn down.

adjudication.rationale:
In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` checks `remaining_time` and `break`s when the deadline is exceeded. That exits the *entire* process-iteration loop, so any subsequent processes are neither waited on nor `terminate()`d. Since `terminate()` is only called inside the loop (after the per-process wait), those skipped processes can remain running even though the strategy teardown completes (`join()` returns). This is directly shown by:
- `for process_index, process in self.processes.items():`
- `if remaining_time <= 0: break`
- termination only happens later: `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:343 — With `timeout=None`, `join()` waits forever on any hung flusher process that never checks `stopped`, and with N processes there are now N chances to block shutdown indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, when `timeout` is `None`, `deadline` stays `None` and the code loops `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or ...)` which becomes an unbounded wait (`while process.is_alive(): time.sleep(0.1)`) for each process. Because the `terminate()` call is after that loop, it is unreachable in the `timeout=None` case, so a stuck flusher process can block shutdown indefinitely; the change to multiple processes (`self.processes` dict) increases the number of processes that could cause this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:247 — Per-process restart counters never reset after a healthy period, so a long-lived consumer with occasional transient failures eventually hits `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and crashes.

adjudication.rationale: In the new per-process health/restart logic, `self.process_restarts[process_index]` is incremented on any unhealthy event in `_ensure_processes_alive()` and is never reset when that process later becomes healthy. The raised error message says "crashed repeatedly", which suggests the counter may have been intended to track consecutive failures, but the diff shows it accumulating across the entire lifetime. However, the diff does not establish that this is incorrect vs. an intentional lifetime cap (and the prior single-counter implementation also did not reset), so it’s a real, diff-grounded concern but not a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — --flusher-processes` is not validated: a negative value makes `num_processes` negative and `process_to_shards_map` empty, so `SpanFlusher.__init__` fails with a KeyError, and 0 silently means one process per shard.

adjudication.rationale: The new click option in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py adds `flusher_processes` with `type=int` but no bounds checking. In `SpanFlusher.__init__` (flusher.py), `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a negative value (truthy) is kept. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can become negative, producing an empty `process_to_shards_map` via `range(self.num_processes)`, and the subsequent loop does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` which will raise a KeyError. Also, `0` is falsy so it falls back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, effectively enabling one process per shard rather than 0 processes, which is an unintuitive/implicit behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62 — The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing because line 15 monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op, so the race between the drift change and `join()` setting `stopped` is still there and the test can still flake.
matched_golden_ids: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate point out that `time.sleep` in `test_consumer.py` is monkeypatched to a no-op earlier in the test, so adding `time.sleep(0.1)` will not actually wait and the race/flakiness remains. This is the same underlying issue and concern about needing a different synchronization/restoring sleep.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:113 — test_flusher_processes_limit only checks structural counts: it never submits spans, never checks that each flusher process flushes its own shards, and never checks the per-process shard mapping (e.g. {0:[0,2],1:[1,3]}).

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions only verify structural properties (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `max_processes/num_processes == 2`, and that the total number of assigned shards sums to 4). The test never drives the flusher by submitting messages/spans, never verifies that flushing works per shard/process, and it does not assert the actual shard distribution in `process_to_shards_map` (only the total count). Given the new nontrivial shard-to-process mapping and per-process buffers introduced in `SpanFlusher.__init__` and `_create_process_for_shards`, this is a concrete coverage gap tied to the diff rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — Nothing tests the per-process restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` (dead process, hang, the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS counter per index). A test would have caught that `isinstance(SpawnProcess, multiprocessing.Process)` is False, so hung spawn processes are never killed before a new one is started.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new restart/health-check logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` (per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`, and restarting via `_create_process_for_shards`), but the added tests only cover process-count limiting (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure aggregation (`test_flusher.py` change). Nothing in the diff exercises the restart paths (dead process, hang via `process_healthy_since`, or hitting `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). However, the finding’s specific claim that `isinstance(SpawnProcess, multiprocessing.Process)` is false is not verifiable from the diff alone and is likely incorrect in typical Python implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337 — Nothing tests `join()` with a timeout across multiple processes. When the deadline passes, the loop `break`s before calling terminate on the remaining processes, and the `isinstance` check at line 346 never matches a SpawnProcess anyway.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks when the deadline has passed (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`), which prevents the code from reaching/terminating any remaining processes in the dict. Given the function then conditionally calls `process.terminate()` for each iterated process, this break yields inconsistent shutdown behavior under a timeout across multiple processes (some may never be waited on or terminated). The diff contains no test exercising join(timeout) with multiple processes to catch this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py:83 — test_backpressure was weakened to `any()` over a single process (one shard), so no test checks that backpressure from one process out of several raises MessageRejected in `submit()`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes flusher backpressure tracking from a single `backpressure_since` value to per-process values (`process_backpressure_since`) and `submit()` now rejects if *any* process has been backpressured too long (loop over `self.process_backpressure_since.values()`). The existing `test_backpressure` assertion was adjusted to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`, but the diff does not show a test that exercises the multi-process case where one process is backpressured and others are not, and verifies `submit()` raises `MessageRejected` based on that single-process condition. That’s a concrete gap in coverage for the new per-process logic, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:433 — Nothing tests the new `--flusher-processes` CLI option or its wiring through the factory. The CLI default is 1 but the factory default is None (one process per shard), so the tests run a configuration that production never uses by default.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py) that explicitly constructs `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., flusher_processes=2, ...)` and asserts `flusher.max_processes == 2` and `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, which directly exercises the new factory parameter and its wiring into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:60 — No edge-case tests for `max_processes` greater than the shard count, zero or negative values (e.g. -1 gives an empty map and then a KeyError at line 66), or empty `assigned_shards`.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` allows negative `max_processes` values (e.g. `-1`) to pass through. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes `-1`, yielding an empty `process_to_shards_map` (`range(-1)`), but the subsequent shard distribution loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and then `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will KeyError because the map has no keys. This is a concrete, diff-grounded crash scenario; the missing edge-case tests are secondary to the underlying defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:299 — Nothing tests adding up Redis memory info across multiple per-process buffers for hard backpressure, or calling `record_stored_segments` on every buffer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new multi-buffer logic in `SpanFlusher.submit`: it now loops `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and aggregates hard-backpressure memory info by extending `memory_infos` from each buffer’s `get_memory_info()` (previously it used a single `self.buffer`). The updated/new tests cover process limiting (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure flag presence (`assert any(x.value ...)`), but nothing in the diff verifies that `record_stored_segments()` is invoked for every per-process buffer or that memory info is correctly summed across multiple buffers for the hard backpressure check. That’s a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced nontrivial behavior, not a proven runtime defect.
